input:
A shell-and-tube exchanger is used to heat crude oil within a refinery preheat train. The duty of the unit is 632 kW. The hot stream enters the exchanger at 180 °C and leaves at 130 °C, while the crude stream enters at 30 °C and leaves at 45 °C. The log-mean temperature difference works out to 116.6 K and the installed area is 23.7 m2, which gives an overall coefficient of 229 W m-2 K-1. This coefficient essentially represents the value that the installed area delivers at the stated duty and the stated log-mean difference, and it is the figure against which a fouling allowance for the train would normally be set.

It should be noted that fouling was assessed on the basis of a single 90-day run, and no cleaning cycle has yet been completed. The coefficient of 229 W m-2 K-1 therefore describes the behaviour of the exchanger over one run from its starting state, and the rate at which fouling continues to build up beyond that run is simply not captured in the record. A second run following cleaning would reveal how much of the resistance the cleaning actually removes and how the coefficient recovers, but on the basis of the present record that recovery remains unmeasured.

A shell-and-tube exchanger heats crude oil in a refinery preheat train. The duty is 632 kW. The hot stream enters at 180 °C and leaves at 130 °C; the crude enters at 30 °C and leaves at 45 °C. The log-mean temperature difference is 116.6 K and the installed area is 23.7 m2, giving an overall coefficient of 229 W m-2 K-1. The coefficient is the value the installed area delivers at the stated duty and the stated log-mean difference, and it is the figure a fouling allowance for the train is set against.

Fouling was assessed from a single 90-day run, and no cleaning cycle has been completed. The coefficient of 229 W m-2 K-1 therefore describes the exchanger over one run from its starting state, and the rate at which fouling builds beyond that run is not in the record. Crude preheat service lays down deposits on both sides of the surface, and the coefficient as reported is a combined figure: it carries the tube-side and shell-side films, the wall, and whatever fouling resistance the run had built by its end, with no separation of the parts. A separation would need a clean-surface reading at the start of the run on the same instrument set. A second run after cleaning would show how much of the resistance the cleaning removes and how the coefficient recovers; on the present record that recovery is unmeasured, and the train is operated on the single-run figure until a post-cleaning run replaces it.
